title: Tuples, named records, dictionaries and sets
outcome: Choose collection representations according to identity, ordering, mutability and lookup needs.

exercises.title: Make one tuple element
exercises.task: Represent a single integer as a tuple.
exercises.answer: The tuple syntax distinguishes a one-field collection from the scalar value.

exercises.title: Name a returned record
exercises.task: Return an ID, score and eligibility field.
exercises.expected: Callers can access fields by their names.
exercises.hint: Prefer explicit semantic labels to remembered positions.
exercises.answer: The representation makes a small fixed schema inspectable.

exercises.title: Preserve multiplicity
exercises.task: Count labels a,b,b before converting to a set.
exercises.expected: Counts are 1 and 2 while the set has two distinct labels.
exercises.hint: Frequency and membership are different questions.
exercises.answer: Deduplication intentionally discards multiplicity and can change a scientific denominator.

exercises.title: Control presentation order
exercises.task: Print a dictionary in an explicitly sorted key order.
exercises.expected: The report follows the chosen ordering rule.
exercises.hint: Do not depend on traversal order.
exercises.answer: Stable presentation requires an explicit contract rather than an incidental implementation order.

exercises.title: Separate absent and zero
exercises.task: Compare a present zero-valued key with an absent key.
exercises.hint: A default value can conceal missingness.
exercises.answer: Only use an absent-to-zero convention when the measurement contract justifies it.

exercises.title: Inspect special keys
exercises.task: Use NaN and both signed zeros as dictionary keys.
exercises.expected: NaN is retrievable and the signed zeros remain distinct in this fixture.
exercises.answer: Dictionary equality semantics should match the application meaning of the keys.
